summary.en: Portuguese 'thank you' matches the speaker's own gender—men say obrigado and women say obrigada.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 1 and 2.

When Jorge unlocks the guesthouse door, Camila says *Obrigada*, and Dona Helena thanks the staff with *Muito obrigada aos dois*. In episode 2, when Camila counts out exact change, Seu Otavio replies *Certinho até a última moeda, obrigado!*

Historically an adjective meaning 'obliged', *obrigado* agrees with the person speaking—not the person being thanked. A man always says *obrigado* regardless of whom he thanks, and a woman always says *obrigada*.

To say 'thank you very much', place invariable *muito* in front (*muito obrigado* / *muito obrigada*). In casual Brazilian moments, you will also hear *valeu!* ('thanks / cheers!').
